newsitem.title: UK: Current aluminium prices a bargain - GNI.
newsitem.headline: Current aluminium prices a bargain - GNI.

text.p: Whether there are production restarts or not current aluminium prices seem to be a long term bargain, said GNI Research in its monthly Commodity Perspective.
It forecast prices in excess of $2,500 a tonne within the next two years versus around $1,700 now.
Capacity restart talk has made the aluminium market nervous and it is possible to interpret recent comments as indicating they could take place in the fourth quarter, GNI said.
Alcoa has indicated that it did not want to restart production until LME stocks were below 500,000 tonnes.
"At the current rate of decline that target will be reached by the end of September," GNI said.
It also pointed out that Reynold's has said that if it was to restart idled capacity then Alcoa would too.
"It does not take too much of a jump in logic to expect the reverse to happen - if Alcoa restarts capacity, then Reynolds will too," GNI said.
Norsk Hydro has indicated it was restarting all its idled capacity by the third quarter putting further competitive pressure on those with spare plant to bring it back in production.

In all there is the potential for close to one million tonnes to be restarted and while it will be needed over the course of 1998, the market impact of the restarts depends upon the speed at which the capacity comes on line.
Unless all of the idled capacity comes on line in one go, it is still likely to leave aluminium in a supply deficit through 1998, GNI said.
By mid-1988 the looming possibility of a capacity squeeze in 1999 may prompt strategic stockpiling which would drive prices sharply higher - possibly surpassing $2,500 a tonne.
